drivingQuestion: Why must the hands be sanctified after urinating?
outcomeNote: the unit breaks off mid-statement of R' Abba

segments.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל הָיָה בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ. בִּשְׁלָמָא רַגְלַיִם מִשּׁוּם נִיצוֹצוֹת, אֶלָּא יָדַיִם מַאי טַעְמָא? אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת,
segments.en: The mishna continues: «This was the principle in the Temple:» Anyone who covers his legs, a euphemism for defecating, must immerse afterward; and anyone who urinates requires sanctification of the hands and feet with water from the basin afterward. The Gemara asks: «Granted,» one who urinates is required to sanctify his «feet, due to drops» of urine that drip on his feet. «However,» with regard to his «hands, what is the reason» that he is required to sanctify them? His hands did not come into contact with anything filthy. «Rabbi Abba said: That is to say» that one learns appropriate conduct from this, namely that

moves.about: lemma: the rule in the Temple on immersion and sanctification after relieving oneself
